When he came out of the tomb, the place was immediately secured automatically. They returned to their house, rejoicing and glorifying God. On the second night, the holy Longinus appeared to the pious woman, saying he was relieved because she had given him his head, and she would be healed from that day. He asked if her son would serve in the heavenly or earthly army. She replied, asking him to enlist her son in the heavenly army. The next day, the youth went to the vineyard to care for the vine. While he was working until the fifth hour, the holy Longinus appeared to him and asked if he wanted to serve in the name of Christ. The youth looked up and saw him like lightning and asked who he was. Longinus replied that he was the one who had been given his head through the youth's mother and wanted to offer the youth to God.

pass_b_english: As the door opened, a light shone throughout the house. The youth entered the tomb with myrrh and aromatics and placed his head with the body. After he exited the tomb, the area was immediately secured. They returned home, rejoicing and glorifying God.

On the second night, the holy Longinus appeared to the pious woman, expressing his gratitude for the return of his head and promising that she would be healed from that day. He asked if her son would serve in the heavenly or earthly army, and she requested that he enlist her son in the heavenly army.

The next day, the youth went to the vineyard to tend to the vine. While working until the fifth hour, the holy Longinus appeared to him, asking if he was willing to serve in the name of Christ. The youth, seeing him as lightning, asked who he was, and Longinus replied that he was the one who had received his head through the youth's mother and now desired to offer the youth to God. The youth responded, 'If this is true, let it be done to me according to your word,' and immediately gave up his spirit.

The mother of the deceased, following her usual routine, had taken some food and was on her way to visit her son in the vineyard. When she arrived, she found him dead. Overcome with grief, she fell to the ground, becoming fainthearted and tearing her tunic, and lay there as if lifeless.

An angel came and strengthened her, asking why she was weeping. She replied that her only son had perished, the fruit of her womb plucked before its time. The angel reassured her, saying that her son was not lost, but was in the care of Jesus Christ. The angel instructed her to go to the village, gather some pious men, and have them carry her son's body to bury it in the tomb where the most faithful Longinus lies, and that after three days she would see her son in the heavenly army.
